name: EBA Guidelines on Restrictive Measures — Sanctions Compliance

articles.title: Scope and subject matter
articles.requirement: The guidelines apply to all credit institutions, investment firms, payment institutions, and electronic money institutions within the EBA's supervisory remit under CRD, PSD2, and EMD. Institutions must ensure compliance with Union and national restrictive measures.

articles.title: Definitions — restrictive measures and designated persons
articles.requirement: Institutions must understand the definitions of restrictive measures, designated persons/entities, asset freeze, economic resources, and related concepts as defined in EU regulations and Council decisions.

articles.title: Internal policies and procedures for restrictive measures
articles.requirement: Institutions must put in place, implement, and maintain up-to-date written internal policies, procedures, and controls for compliance with all applicable Union and national restrictive measures.

articles.title: Integration with existing compliance framework
articles.requirement: Restrictive measures policies must be integrated with the institution's existing AML/CFT framework while being distinct and specifically addressing sanctions compliance, with clear escalation and decision-making procedures.

articles.title: Proportionality and risk-based application
articles.requirement: Policies, procedures, and controls must be proportionate to the size, nature, scale, and complexity of the institution's activities and its exposure to restrictive measures risk.

articles.title: Management body — overall responsibility
articles.requirement: The management body in its management function is responsible for approving the institution's restrictive measures implementation strategy and must monitor its effective implementation and execution. Responsibility goes beyond formal endorsement.

articles.title: Management body — supervisory function oversight
articles.requirement: The management body in its supervisory function must oversee the institution's compliance with restrictive measures, including reviewing the adequacy and effectiveness of policies, procedures, and controls at regular intervals.

articles.title: Designation of senior manager
articles.requirement: Institutions must appoint a senior staff member responsible for the operational implementation of restrictive measures compliance, performing functions and tasks including day-to-day oversight, escalation, and reporting to the management body.

articles.title: Senior manager — independence and resources
articles.requirement: The senior manager responsible for restrictive measures must have adequate authority, independence, and resources to effectively perform their role. The role may be combined with the AML/CFT compliance officer role where proportionate.

articles.title: Senior manager — tasks and reporting
articles.requirement: The senior manager must regularly report to the management body on the institution's restrictive measures compliance, including exposure assessment results, screening effectiveness, identified breaches, and remediation actions taken.

articles.title: Restrictive measures exposure assessment — requirement
articles.requirement: Institutions must carry out a restrictive measures exposure assessment to identify, assess, and understand their exposure to the risk of breaching or being used to circumvent restrictive measures. The assessment must inform the types of controls and measures applied.

articles.title: Exposure assessment — risk factors
articles.requirement: The exposure assessment must consider at minimum three dimensions: geographical risks (jurisdictions subject to restrictive measures), customer and counterparty risks (exposure to designated persons/sectors), and product and distribution channel risks.

articles.title: Exposure assessment — information sources
articles.requirement: The exposure assessment must be based on a sufficiently diverse range of information sources including EU sanctions lists, national designations, UN resolutions, guidance from competent authorities, and relevant sectoral information.

articles.title: Exposure assessment — frequency and updates
articles.requirement: The exposure assessment must be reviewed and updated at least annually and whenever there are significant changes to the institution's business, customer base, or the restrictive measures landscape, including new designations or sanctions regimes.

articles.title: Screening — general requirements
articles.requirement: Institutions must implement adequate and reliable screening systems and processes to identify whether any of their customers, beneficial owners, transactions, or business relationships involve designated persons, entities, or restricted activities.

articles.title: Screening — customer and counterparty screening
articles.requirement: Institutions must screen all customers, beneficial owners, and counterparties against applicable sanctions lists at onboarding and on an ongoing basis, including when sanctions lists are updated. Screening must cover the full customer lifecycle.

articles.title: Screening — transaction screening
articles.requirement: Institutions must screen transactions in real time or near-real time to detect transactions involving designated persons, sanctioned jurisdictions, or restricted goods and services. Both incoming and outgoing transactions must be screened.

articles.title: Screening system adequacy and calibration
articles.requirement: Screening systems must be fit-for-purpose, tailored to the institution's risk profile and business activities. Systems must be regularly calibrated, tested, and validated to ensure they produce effective results with manageable false positive rates.

articles.title: Screening — list management and updates
articles.requirement: Institutions must ensure that sanctions list updates are implemented without undue delay. The institution must have procedures to ensure prompt incorporation of new designations, de-listings, and amendments to existing designations.

articles.title: Alert management and investigation
articles.requirement: Institutions must establish clear procedures for the timely analysis, investigation, and resolution of screening alerts. Confirmed matches must be escalated immediately. Investigation timelines must be documented and monitored.

articles.title: Screening — documentation and audit trail
articles.requirement: Institutions must maintain a complete audit trail of screening activities including alerts generated, investigation steps taken, decisions made, and the rationale for match or no-match determinations.

articles.title: Freezing obligations — immediate action
articles.requirement: Upon identifying a confirmed match with a designated person or entity, institutions must freeze all funds and economic resources belonging to, owned, held, or controlled by the designated person without delay, and must not make funds available.

articles.title: Freezing — notification to authorities
articles.requirement: Institutions must notify the relevant competent authorities without delay of any frozen funds or economic resources, providing full details of the designated person, the nature and value of frozen assets, and the circumstances of identification.

articles.title: Freezing — ongoing obligations
articles.requirement: Frozen funds must remain frozen until the designation is lifted or a specific licence or authorisation is obtained from the competent authority. Institutions must monitor and maintain frozen accounts, preventing any unauthorised transactions.

articles.title: Designation verification and beneficial ownership
articles.requirement: Institutions must take adequate steps to verify whether customers or counterparties are designated persons, including assessment of beneficial ownership structures, nominee arrangements, and complex ownership chains that may obscure designated persons.

articles.title: Circumvention — risk identification
articles.requirement: Institutions must identify and assess the risk that their products, services, or infrastructure are used to circumvent or evade restrictive measures, including through use of intermediaries, front companies, or complex transaction structures.

articles.title: Circumvention — preventive controls
articles.requirement: Institutions must implement controls to detect and prevent circumvention attempts, including monitoring for structured transactions, unusual patterns, use of third parties to obscure the involvement of designated persons, and evasion of sectoral sanctions.

articles.title: Circumvention — reporting obligations
articles.requirement: Institutions must report any suspected circumvention or evasion attempts to competent authorities without delay, including attempted transactions that were prevented. Staff must be aware of circumvention typologies and red flags.

articles.title: Training programme — scope and frequency
articles.requirement: Institutions must establish a training programme on restrictive measures compliance tailored to the specific roles and responsibilities of staff. Training must be delivered at onboarding and refreshed regularly, at minimum annually.

articles.title: Training — role-specific content
articles.requirement: Training content must be adapted to staff functions: front-office staff must understand screening and escalation procedures; compliance staff must understand investigation, freezing, and reporting; management must understand governance responsibilities and strategic oversight.

articles.title: Training — competent authority verification
articles.requirement: Competent authorities must be able to verify the adequacy of training programmes, including content, frequency, attendance records, and assessments. Institutions must retain evidence of training delivery and effectiveness.

articles.title: Record-keeping requirements
articles.requirement: Institutions must maintain comprehensive records of all restrictive measures compliance activities including screening results, alert investigations, freezing actions, reports to authorities, exposure assessments, and policy documents for at least five years.

articles.title: Reporting to competent authorities
articles.requirement: Institutions must immediately report to competent authorities any identified breaches of restrictive measures, confirmed matches, frozen assets, and suspected circumvention attempts. Regular reporting on compliance activities must also be provided as required.

articles.title: Reporting — breach remediation
articles.requirement: Where deficiencies or breaches are identified, institutions must conduct root-cause analysis, implement corrective actions, and report remediation progress to the management body and competent authorities. Continuous improvement must be demonstrated.

articles.title: Outsourcing of restrictive measures functions
articles.requirement: Where institutions outsource restrictive measures compliance functions (e.g., screening), they remain fully responsible for compliance. Outsourcing arrangements must ensure the service provider meets all requirements and allows supervisory access.

articles.title: Outsourcing — due diligence and monitoring
articles.requirement: Institutions must conduct due diligence on service providers, establish clear contractual requirements for restrictive measures compliance, and monitor the provider's performance on an ongoing basis including screening system effectiveness.

articles.title: Group-wide application
articles.requirement: Parent institutions must ensure that restrictive measures policies, procedures, and controls are applied consistently across the group, including subsidiaries and branches in third countries, to the extent permitted by local law.

articles.title: Group-wide — information sharing and escalation
articles.requirement: Groups must establish mechanisms for sharing information about designated persons, frozen assets, and circumvention risks across entities. Group-level escalation procedures must be in place for significant restrictive measures events.

articles.title: PSP screening — scope and application
articles.requirement: Payment service providers must implement specific screening systems and controls for transfers of funds under Regulation (EU) 2023/1113, ensuring that both originator and beneficiary information is screened against applicable sanctions lists.

articles.title: PSP screening — system selection and adequacy
articles.requirement: PSPs must select screening systems that are adequate and reliable for the volume and nature of their payment transactions. Systems must be capable of screening in real time or near-real time and must handle all payment channels and instruments.

articles.title: PSP screening — dataset and parameters
articles.requirement: PSPs must define screening parameters and assess whether the data they hold on originators and beneficiaries is sufficiently accurate, up to date, and detailed to enable effective screening. Fuzzy matching and transliteration capabilities must be appropriate.

articles.title: PSP screening — testing and annual review
articles.requirement: PSPs must conduct in-depth effectiveness testing confirming current sanctions lists are loaded, full customer and transaction screening is operational, and automatic transaction suspension capabilities function correctly. Reviews must be performed at least annually.

articles.title: CASP screening — scope and application
articles.requirement: Crypto-asset service providers must implement specific screening systems and controls for transfers of crypto-assets, ensuring that originator and beneficiary information is screened against applicable sanctions lists, including for self-hosted wallet transfers.

articles.title: CASP screening — system selection and blockchain considerations
articles.requirement: CASPs must select screening systems capable of handling the specific characteristics of crypto-asset transfers including blockchain-based transactions, pseudonymous addresses, and cross-chain transfers. Blockchain analytics tools may be necessary to meet screening obligations.

articles.title: CASP screening — testing, calibration, and reporting
articles.requirement: CASPs must test and calibrate screening systems using live sanctions data and manipulated records before deployment. Deficiencies must be immediately reported with root-cause analysis. Continuous improvement with board-level oversight must be demonstrated.
